sections.h2: Which Crow Wing County office handles property tax?
sections.html:
In Crow Wing County the Land Services Department does the work of assessing values and collecting tax. It sits at 322 Laurel Street in Brainerd, the county seat, and the main number is 218-824-1010.

Land Services mails bills, takes payments, answers valuation questions and keeps the field books and parcel records that the public can research on the lower level of its building. The county's Property Search website shows parcel data, and a duplicate tax statement can be pulled there by parcel ID or address.

sections.h2: What is Crow Wing County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Crow Wing County is a lake country in east central Minnesota: 999 square miles of land, about 417 recognized lakes, the Mississippi River running through it, and gently rolling, mostly wooded ground. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate puts the population at 69,132, up 4.6% from the 2020 base.

  • Communities on the county's list include Brainerd, Baxter, Crosby, Crosslake, Garrison, Nisswa, Pequot Lakes, Breezy Point, Deerwood and Fort Ripley.
  • The Census Bureau counts 44,306 housing units and 29,402 households, and Wikipedia's 2020 figures show 32.9% of housing units vacant, which points to a large stock of cabins.
  • Owner-occupied homes are 77.0% of occupied housing, with a median value of $306,800 (2020 to 2024).
  • Median household income is $72,589, and 26.8% of residents are 65 or older.
  • The Census Bureau reports 625 building permits for 2025.

Brainerd began in 1870 when the Northern Pacific Railroad picked the site for its Mississippi River crossing, and it took the county seat from the earlier trading village of Crow Wing. Because so many parcels here are lakeshore, classification matters: a homestead and a seasonal cabin are taxed under different rules.

sections.h2: When are Crow Wing County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate taxes are due May 15 for the first half and October 15 for the second half. Agricultural land has until November 15 for the second half, and mobile home taxes are due August 31 and November 15.

Resorts and businesses that earn more than 60% of gross income between May and August can file an affidavit to push the first-half date to May 31, and the affidavit must accompany the payment. All 2026 real estate dates have now passed, so any balance from this year is already carrying penalty.

Taxes become delinquent if they are not paid by December 31 of the year they come due. For delinquent years, the county asks you to call Land Services at 218-824-1010 before paying so you pay the right amount, and it notes that payments are applied to the newest years first under Minnesota Statutes section 280.39.

sections.h2: What does a late payment cost in Crow Wing County?
sections.html:
The county posts a penalty table set by the state, and the first half is where it grows fastest. The table below shows what Crow Wing County lists for an unpaid first half.

Manufactured homes carry an 8% penalty from September 1 on the first half, and personal property is at 8% from May 16. Section 279.01 also lets the treasurer waive the penalty once when a mailed check was postmarked within one business day of the due date.

sections.h2: How do you pay taxes in Crow Wing County?
sections.html:
You can pay online, at the counter, in a drop box or by mail.

  • Online: E-check costs $1.95 and a card costs 2.35% of the payment or $1.95, whichever is greater, with a $50,000 limit. The processor collects those fees, not the county, and credit takes three to four days to post.
  • You need the 8-digit parcel number for each parcel, and a full year is paid by choosing Pay Full Year.
  • In person: the customer service counter is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and a drop box outside the office is available at any time.
  • By mail: send the remittance stub and payment to Land Services, 322 Laurel Street Ste 15, Brainerd, MN 56401.

sections.h2: How does Crow Wing County value property and handle appeals?
sections.html:
State law has the county revalue property every year and keep assessed values between 90% and 105% of market value. The assessors also inspect each property every five years and verify permits. Valuation rests on sales of comparable properties plus the land, size, quality and condition of the building, and classification follows current use.

The county describes a two-option appeal path. Option One is the Board of Appeal and Equalization: you go first to your local board or open book meeting, and then to the County Board of Appeal and Equalization, where you must call ahead to get on the agenda. If your city or township no longer has a local board, an open book meeting comes before the county board. Option Two is the Minnesota Tax Court.

  • Meeting times and places are printed on your Notice of Valuation and Classification.
  • You may appear in person, send a letter, or use a representative you authorize.
  • Under section 278.01 a petition and proof of service must be filed with the district court by April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

sections.h2: Which relief programs does Crow Wing County point owners to?
sections.html:
The county's Taxes page links to Minnesota Department of Revenue guidance for owners who may qualify for a lower bill. Several of them depend on filing before a deadline, so ask Land Services which ones fit your parcel.

  • Homestead classification and the homestead market value exclusion for owner-occupied houses.
  • Special homestead classification for owners who are blind or disabled.
  • Senior citizen property tax deferral.
  • Market value exclusion for veterans with a disability.
  • 2c managed forest land and the Sustainable Forest Incentive Act.
  • Green Acres and rural preserve deferral for agricultural and rural vacant land, plus special agricultural homestead.
  • Property tax refunds.

A seller who is behind on tax can also pay part of a bill. The treasurer may accept less than the full installment, and under section 279.01 the money goes to the oldest unpaid installment first. A payment that falls short is applied to accrued penalty before tax. A partial payment does not waive the minimum payment needed to keep an appeal alive.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when a Crow Wing County house sells?
sections.html:
Before the deed is recorded, the auditor checks for delinquent tax and stamps it "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered" (section 272.12). The deed also needs a certificate of real estate value if the price is above $3,000 (section 272.115), and homestead classification comes off the property for the next assessment year until the buyer applies and qualifies.

Ask Land Services for a payoff figure for each parcel, since a lake property sale often includes several. The assessing office also lists tax relief programs that can matter to a new owner, such as 2c managed forest, disabled veterans, Green Acres, homesteading and rural preserve.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Crow Wing County property taxes?
faqs.a: You pay Land Services at 322 Laurel Street Ste 15 in Brainerd, online, by mail or in a drop box. The counter is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone is 218-824-1010.

faqs.q: What are the Crow Wing County due dates?
faqs.a: Real estate is due May 15 and October 15, agricultural second half on November 15, and mobile homes on August 31 and November 15. The 2026 real estate dates have passed, so the next one is the first half in May 2027.

faqs.q: How much is the late penalty on a Crow Wing County homestead?
faqs.a: It starts at 2% on an unpaid first half after May 15 and reaches 8% by October 1, according to the county's table. Non-homestead property starts at 4% and tops out at 12%.

faqs.q: Can I challenge my Crow Wing County valuation now?
faqs.a: The local and county board meetings for the 2026 value are finished. A Tax Court or district court petition on taxes payable in 2027 is due April 30, 2027, so call Land Services at 218-824-1010 and ask for the assessor.

faqs.q: Do delinquent Crow Wing County taxes need to be paid before a sale?
faqs.a: Yes, delinquent taxes must be cleared before the deed can be recorded. Call Land Services before paying them online, because the county wants staff to confirm the right amount and avoid extra penalty.
